name: Palantir

Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Heavy — standard LeetCode-style problems mixed with deliberately ambiguous, non-standard prompts that reward structuring ambiguity over memorized answers
rounds: Recruiter screen (~30 min): background, motivation, and (distinctively) comfort discussing Palantir’s work on civil-liberties-adjacent government/defense contracts
Online assessment (for some pipelines): coding challenges testing analytical ability
Technical phone screen(s) (45-90 min, 1-2 rounds): live coding plus algorithmic questions

Onsite/virtual loop (3-5 rounds, up to 3 hrs each): at least one coding round (DS&A), a system design round, a "decomposition/learning" round (an intentionally vague, open-ended problem — e.g. a Mars-base planning prompt or a broken-API debugging exercise — where interviewers give minimal guidance on purpose), and a behavioral round
extraTopics: Turning ambiguity into structure — this is explicitly what Palantir is reported to select for, more than polished right answers
Being comfortable discussing civil liberties and government/defense work, which comes up as a genuine values-fit topic, not small talk
Software Engineer.notes: Palantir’s Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) role has a distinct, more client-facing loop not fully covered by the sources reviewed here.
